name: Shortfall-minimizing allocation rules

label: theorem:inner-approx
title: Theorem
body_md:
For any shortfall-minimizing allocation rule, any feasible solution to Problem~\eqref{eq:inner} is feasible for Problem~\eqref{eq:opt-shared}.
\label{theorem:inner-approx}
head: environment

label: eq:inner-approx-lb-simpl
title: Proof
body_md:
We will write $\mathcal{E} := \left\{ \sum_{i} (\xi_i - x_i)_+ \leq s \right\}$ and
$\mathcal{E}_{i} := \left\{ x_i + f_{i}(\bm{x}, \bm{\xi}, s) \geq \xi_i \right\}$ for
brevity. We have
\begin{align}
  
    \ifx\\\\
        \mathrm{Pr} \left( \mathcal{E}_i \right)
    \else
        \mathrm{Pr}_{} \left( \mathcal{E}_i \right)
    \fi

  &= 
    \ifx\\\\
        \mathrm{Pr} \left( \mathcal{E}_i \cap \mathcal{E} \right)
    \else
        \mathrm{Pr}_{} \left( \mathcal{E}_i \cap \mathcal{E} \right)
    \fi
 + 
    \ifx\\\\
        \mathrm{Pr} \left( \mathcal{E}_i \cap \mathcal{E}^c \right)
    \else
        \mathrm{Pr}_{} \left( \mathcal{E}_i \cap \mathcal{E}^c \right)
    \fi
 \notag \\
  & \geq
  
    \ifx\\\\
        \mathrm{Pr} \left( \mathcal{E}_i \cap \mathcal{E} \right)
    \else
        \mathrm{Pr}_{} \left( \mathcal{E}_i \cap \mathcal{E} \right)
    \fi

  \notag \\
  &=
  
    \ifx\\\\
        \mathrm{Pr} \left( x_i + f_{i}(\bm{x}, \bm{\xi}, s) \geq \xi_i \mid \mathcal{E} \right)
    \else
        \mathrm{Pr}_{} \left( x_i + f_{i}(\bm{x}, \bm{\xi}, s) \geq \xi_i \mid \mathcal{E} \right)
    \fi

  \cdot 
    \ifx\\\\
        \mathrm{Pr} \left( \mathcal{E} \right)
    \else
        \mathrm{Pr}_{} \left( \mathcal{E} \right)
    \fi
 \label{eq:inner-approx-lb-simpl} \\
  &= 
    \ifx\\\\
        \mathrm{Pr} \left( \mathcal{E} \right)
    \else
        \mathrm{Pr}_{} \left( \mathcal{E} \right)
    \fi
,
  \label{eq:inner-approx-lb-1}
\end{align}
using~\eqref{eq:allocation-rule-property} in~\eqref{eq:inner-approx-lb-simpl} to
deduce that the conditional probability $
    \ifx\\\\
        \mathrm{Pr} \left( \mathcal{E}_{i} \mid \mathcal{E} \right)
    \else
        \mathrm{Pr}_{} \left( \mathcal{E}_{i} \mid \mathcal{E} \right)
    \fi
 = 1$. Since $\alpha \geq \alpha_i$ and the
choice of index $i$ was arbitrary, the desired claim follows.
